findings.issue: The review class is the only owner of the convergence phrase `findings stop changing`, so a research-framed request that uses it resolves to the review loop in one silent step, with no clarify and no ambiguity flag; the same prompt without that clause defers. That breaks the hub's own policy that an unclear deep-loop intent asks (routerPolicy.defaultMode null, ambiguityDelta 1), and skill-hub-routing section 4, because the phrase catches traffic the selected mode cannot serve. Nothing on the research side scores: bare `research` is in no class, so review wins by 4 against 0. Either drop the phrase from review-aliases so those prompts defer, or add a convergence phrase to research-aliases so the delta defers; ROUTER.md section 3 REVIEW INTENT_SIGNALS carries the identical keyword and must move with it (the two stage-two keyword sets are equal today). Not introduced here: hub-router.json only gained the version line in this diff.

findings.issue: The new expansive-depth feature contributes no routing vocabulary at any stage: `expansive`, `frontier`, `sub-target` and `depth mode` occur zero times in SKILL.md's keyword line, description.json's keywords, hub-router.json's vocabularyClasses, mode-registry.json's aliases, ROUTER.md's INTENT_SIGNALS and graph-metadata.json's intent_signals. A probe written from the feature's own documented wording therefore lands on a skill that has no such feature, silently: top-1 sk-code at score 0.6528, confidence 0.8709 (above the 0.8 bar), ambiguous false, compiled route sk-code-review; and top-1 sk-doc at 0.08 for a second one. The two feature probes that do reach the hub win on their mode words, not on the feature's. A complete fix is a dual write: graph-metadata.json intent_signals (stage one, outside this change's file set) plus this file's vocabularyClasses (stage two, to choose research vs review).

findings.issue: Confirmed cause of the failed S9-command-references row, and it is not a defect in any /deep:* command file. The validator requires every literal repo-relative token to exist on disk, and this line names `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/database/access-telemetry.json`. That directory is gitignored (.gitignore:431) and is created at runtime: shared/config.ts derives TELEMETRY_STORE_DIR as `<skill root>/runtime/database`, so the YAML points at the right place but at a path a clean checkout cannot contain. Either teach validate-command-references.cjs that this declared state path is data rather than a skill asset, or reword the line so it stops reading as a file reference. Outside this change's scope.
